history.summary: Freehold 764 sqft 2BR in a tiny 21-unit 2017 boutique walk-up off Geylang (D14, near Kaki Bukit). The algo's headline -25.6% cheap signal is a data quirk: it rests on only 12 appreciation txns, psf_cohort_txns=0, and a negative -2.68% CAGR. Verified data shows the project trades around $1,510 median psf, so $1,440 psf is mildly below median but the -25.6% bargain is illusory.
history.rating_rationale: The standout -25.6% age-adjusted cheapness does not survive scrutiny: Qube Suites is a 21-unit project with ~18 lifetime sale transactions, only 12 appreciation comps, and psf_cohort_txns=0 — far too thin to trust a 25% discount read. Verified web data puts the median at ~$1,510 psf (highest $1,656 psf for a 420sqft unit), so the $1,440 psf asking on a 764 sqft 2BR is at best modestly below median, NOT a quarter cheaper. Trailing appreciation is negative (-2.68%). Freehold is not a forward edge per the backtest. The fundamental problem is liquidity: a 21-unit walk-up with no facilities-driven appeal and Kaki Bukit (not city-fringe MRT) as the nearest station has very thin resale demand, a serious risk for a 5-7yr exit. The verdict is a quirk-driven cheap signal masking an illiquid micro-project.

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Poor outlook. Trailing CAGR is negative (-2.68%) and the cheap signal is a thin-data artifact, not a genuine value entry; freehold offers no forward edge, and the micro-project's illiquidity is a material drag on any 5-7yr capital outcome.
